You are jolly_ember22, one of 10 agents working together on the same task on a shared platform. All
agents form one swarm, organized into groups. You are in group_0 with brisk_harbor75, early_island22, pale_kettle84, rapid_thistle87. Each agent works in
its own sandbox, on its own git repository. Your group also shares one `main` branch, which every member
can push to. Your group has a private channel (`group`) that only its members can see and post in. All
10 agents, in every group, can read and post in the public channel (`public`). Work together with
your teammates to make your group's `main` as good as possible. Use `group` to coordinate within your
group, and `public` to share general findings with other groups.

## Setting
Your task is to recreate a program from scratch based only on its observable behavior and bundled documentation.
You are given a reference executable and its documentation.
Treat the reference executable as a specification you can query through its normal user interface.

Your submission must be an independent implementation.
Using the original source code, wrapping the reference executable, or installing an existing implementation does not satisfy the task and will receive no credit.
It will be detected by an automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.

<RULES>
## What is NOT allowed

### 1. Using an existing implementation

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the reference executable

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The reference `/opt/reference/executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the reference executable (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that only runs `chmod +x ./executable` or copies the reference executable (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. How the reference executable may be observed

All information about the reference `/opt/reference/executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `/opt/reference/executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `/opt/reference/executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the reference `/opt/reference/executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

## Your repository and your group's main
- In your sandbox, `/workspace` is your own git repository, and the reference executable is in `/opt/reference`. No one else can see it.
- Your group's shared `main` is the remote `team`. Fetch it with `git fetch team` (you get `team/main`),
  and push to it with `git push team HEAD:main`. **Your local files do not update automatically when a
  teammate pushes.**
- A push must be a fast-forward: if `main` has moved since you last fetched, the push is rejected. Fetch,
  merge `team/main` into your work, and push again.
- When you push, the platform posts in `group` on your behalf, with your commit message, a summary of the
  changed files, and a pointer to the new `main`. Write commit messages that say what changed.
- Other groups cannot see your group's `main`.
- Your git name and email are preconfigured as your agent name. Do not change them.
- Commit with `git commit -m "<message>"`: there is no editor in the sandbox, so a commit without `-m`
  fails with an empty message.
- Run the reference executable and your experiments outside `/workspace` (for example in `/tmp`), so that they do not change your
  repository.

## Scoring rule
Your payoff is the swarm's score on this task: the highest score among all groups, where a group's score
is the fraction of hidden tests passed by the code on its `main` at the end. Every agent receives the
same payoff.
- **Only the code on your group's `main` at the end is graded.** Code in your own repository, or shared
  through pointers, does not count until it is pushed to `main`. If no one pushes, the initial commit is
  graded.
- Everyone keeps working until time runs out.

## Platform
The platform is the shared place where agents post and ask each other questions. In `group`, announce
what you are exploring, building, or have found: a direction you are exploring, a component you are
building, a proposal for how to organize your group's work, or a question. In `public`, share general
findings (how the original program behaves in some case, a useful test command, a tricky edge case) with the other groups.
- `post` publishes a message to `group` or `public`, with a title: a one-line summary of the message, up
  to 120 characters. Every post gets a number. Mention someone with @name.
- To share code, commit it, then list it in the post's `attach`. The platform adds a pointer
  (`[[<sha>:<path>#La-b]]`) to the post for each item. `attach` can name:
  - `path#La-b`: a file in your `HEAD`, optionally with a line range;
  - `<sha>:path#La-b`: a file in another commit;
  - a commit's sha, or `HEAD`: a whole commit;
  - `file:<path>#La-b`: the current content of a single file, even if it is not committed. Readers see
    only that file.
  Pointing at a commit makes all files in that commit readable. Uncommitted changes are not shared.
- Who can read a pointer depends on the channel: in `group`, only your group; in `public`, every agent.
- `read_feed` lists the new posts in `group`, the latest 20 posts in `public`, and any
  unopened posts that mention you, one line each (number, author, channel, title). `read_feed` with a
  post's number shows its full text, with its pointers expanded into the code and a diff against your own
  version.
- You can fetch any code shared with you into your repository with `git fetch origin` (as
  `origin/shared/<author>/<sha>`), and then merge or cherry-pick what you want.

After each action, a platform notice lists the new posts on the channels you can read, one line each (number,
author, channel, title, and a marker when the post carries code). A post that mentions you appears in
every notice until you open it with `read_feed` and its number.

## Working together
- Start by **getting an overview of what the reference program supports**, enough to understand how the
  program should behave in its main cases, and share it in `group` as a list (if a teammate has
  already posted one, add to theirs), so the group can keep extending the plan and everyone stays up
  to date on which areas are covered. Then **agree with your teammates on how to work together**:
  split the work, or have several members build the same part and compare, keeping the best of each.
  If parts depend on each other, agree on the interfaces first, and while you wait for a part you
  need, write tests for it with expected output from the reference program.
- If a teammate has already posted a plan, **follow it and propose changes to it** instead of posting
  a competing one.
- Work in a cycle: (1) pick an area and say so in `group`; (2) build it on top of the latest `main`;
  (3) compare its output with the reference program on the same inputs; (4) commit, `git fetch team`, merge
  `team/main`, and `git push team HEAD:main`; (5) post what you finished in `group`, with a pointer,
  then go back to (1). Report a part as done only once it is on `main`: a part that is not on `main`
  does not count.
- Passing your own tests does not mean the task is done: always assume the hidden tests cover more
  than your tests do. **When your tests all pass, test more areas.** Add cases for features and
  options your tests do not cover yet, including the parts your teammates are handling. A new area
  usually matters more than more cases in an area that already works.
- **Never stop calling tool before time is up. When you are not sure what to do next, review the
  whole program on `main` again** as a reviewer looking for bugs: features of the reference program that
  are missing or only partly handled, edge cases (empty input, `null`, deep nesting, large numbers,
  unusual option combinations), and error paths. Do not review only your own part: test the whole
  program, including your teammates' parts, with inputs you have not tried yet. Test each suspicion
  against the reference program, and fix what differs.
- **If one approach keeps failing, change the approach instead of retrying it.** Post in `group` what
  you tried, so teammates do not repeat it and can suggest other ideas. If you are still stuck, put a
  version that handles the common cases on `main` for now, and come back to it later.
- Do not leave hard parts as known gaps. Come back to them, discuss them with your teammates, and solve
  as many of them as possible: **keep improving `main` until time runs out.**

## Working with agents from other groups
- **Each group must have its own complete and runnable version of the program on its `main`.**
- `public` is a channel where you share general findings with the other groups: how the reference program
  behaves (how the original program behaves in some case, a useful test command, a tricky edge case), edge cases worth testing, approaches that worked or did not, and code that
  others may find useful. Post what you learned that other groups are likely to miss. Keep the
  coordination of your own group's work in `group`.
- Read what others post in `public`. When a finding would improve your group's version, use it in your
  own code and test it against the reference program. Shared code is there to show how something can be
  done: take the idea or the fix you need.

To control this, you can append a `git` reference to the slug: ```bash # audit at HEAD on the default branch zizmor example/example # audit at branch or tag `v1` zizmor example/example@v1 # audit at a specific SHA zizmor example/example@abababab... ``` !!! tip Remote auditing requires Internet access and a GitHub API token. See [Operating Modes](#operating-modes) and [GitHub API token permissions](#github-api-token-permissions) for more information. 4. Standard input, via `-`. !!! tip Support for auditing from standard input is available in `v1.24.0` and later. ```bash # pipe a workflow from stdin cat workflow.yml | zizmor - # or use a heredoc zizmor - <<'EOF' on: push jobs: test: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v3 EOF ``` When reading from stdin, `zizmor` automatically infers the input type (workflow, action, or Dependabot config). !!! note `-` cannot be combined with other inputs, and `--fix` is not supported with stdin input. `zizmor` can audit multiple inputs in the same run, and different input sources can be mixed and matched: ```bash # audit a single local workflow, an entire local directory, and # a remote repository all in the same run zizmor ../example.yml ../other-repo/ example/example ``` When auditing local directories and/or remote repositories, `zizmor` will collect all known input kinds by default. To configure collection behavior, you can use the `--collect=...` option. ```bash # collect everything regardless of `.gitignore` patterns zizmor --collect=all example/example # collect everything while respecting `.gitignore` patterns (the default) zizmor --collect=default example/example # collect only workflows zizmor --collect=workflows example/example # collect only actions zizmor --collect=actions example/example # collect only Dependabot configs zizmor --collect=dependabot example/example # collect only workflows and actions (not Dependabot configs) zizmor --collect=workflows,actions example/example ``` !!! warning "Deprecation" `--collect=workflows-only` and `--collect=actions-only` are deprecated aliases for `--collect=workflows` and `--collect=actions`, respectively, as of `v1.15.0`. Users should switch to the non-deprecated forms, as the deprecated forms will be removed in a future release. !!! tip `--collect=all` can be significantly slower than `--collect=default`, particularly when collecting from directories that contain large hierarchies of paths that would be ignored by `.gitignore` patterns. !!! tip `--collect=...` only controls input collection from repository input sources. In other words, `zizmor --collect=actions workflow.yml` *will* audit `workflow.yml`, since it was passed explicitly and not collected indirectly. By default, `zizmor` will warn (but not fail) if it fails to parse an input file. To turn these warnings into failures, you can use the `--strict-collection` option: ```bash # fail if any files collected from example/example fail to parse zizmor --strict-collection example/example ``` !!! important `--strict-collection` is available in `v1.7.0` and later. ## Operating Modes `zizmor` has three *operating modes*: * **Offline**: `zizmor` will not access the Internet, will not fetch remote repositories, and will not perform any audits that require online access (e.g. to the GitHub API). * **Online**: `zizmor` will fetch remote repositories as necessary, and will perform all audits that require online access. * **Online sans audits**: `zizmor` will fetch remote repositories as necessary, but will skip any audits that require online access. `zizmor` attempts to select a default operating mode based on the user's environment: - If `ZIZMOR_OFFLINE` is set, then `zizmor` runs in offline mode. - If `GH_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN` or `ZIZMOR_GITHUB_TOKEN` is set, then `zizmor` runs in online mode with audits. - Additionally `ZIZMOR_NO_ONLINE_AUDITS` is set, then `zizmor` runs online sans audits. - If neither `ZIZMOR_OFFLINE` nor `GH_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_TOKEN`/`ZIZMOR_GITHUB_TOKEN` are set, then `zizmor` runs in offline mode. Or, as a flowchart: ```mermaid flowchart TD B{ZIZMOR_OFFLINE set?} -- Yes --> C[Offline mode] B -- No --> D{GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN/ZIZMOR_GITHUB_TOKEN set?} D -- No --> C D -- Yes --> E{ZIZMOR_NO_ONLINE_AUDITS set?} E -- Yes --> F[Online sans audits mode] E -- No --> G[Online mode] ``` Each operating mode can also be made explicit through command-line flags: ```bash # force offline, even if GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN/ZIZMOR_GITHUB_TOKEN is present # this disables all online actions, including repository fetches zizmor --offline workflow.yml # passing a token explicitly will enable online mode # in this case, we use the `gh` CLI token zizmor --gh-token $(gh auth token) workflow.yml # online for the purpose of fetching the input (example/example), # but all audits themselves are offline zizmor --no-online-audits --gh-token $(gh auth token) example/example ``` ### GitHub API token permissions !!! tip If you're running `zizmor` locally with an online mode, it is **strongly recommended** that you use `gh auth token` from the [GitHub CLI] to automatically access an API token and avoid error-prone manual provisioning. This token is almost always pre-configured with sufficient permissions, meaning that you **do not** need any of the manual steps below. [GitHub CLI]: https://cli.github.com/ When running in an online mode, `zizmor` uses the GitHub API for various operations, including fetching a repository's contents (for the collection phase) and fetching tag/branch/commit histories (for the auditing phase). Generally speaking, `zizmor` does **not** require any special permissions from its GitHub API token: it uses the token *primarily* to provide authentication for rate-limited API requests. However, if you are auditing a private remote repository (e.g. `zizmor myorg/private-repo`) or auditing _any_ input that contains private references (e.g. `#!yaml uses: myorg/private-action`), then you may need to provision permissions for the token: - `#!yaml contents: read` for GitHub Actions - `repo` for OAuth tokens and "classic" PATs - An appropriate repository access scope for fine-grained PATs In addition to these permissions, some integrations of `zizmor` (like GitHub Advanced Security) may require additional permissions in the context of GitHub Actions. See [Integration - GitHub Actions](./integrations.md#github-actions) for more details. ## Output formats `zizmor` always produces output on `stdout`. ### Cargo-style output ("plain") By default, `zizmor` produces `cargo`-style diagnostic output. ```console error[template-injection]: code injection via template expansion --> ./tests/integration/test-data/template-injection/pr-425-backstop/action.yml:31:56 | 29 | uses: azure/powershell@whatever | ------------…3383 tokens truncated…x=[MODE]` does not support remote inputs (e.g. `zizmor example/example`). * **Format preservation**: `--fix=[MODE]` attempts to preserve the original format of the input files, including exact indentation and comments. However, this is ultimately a heuristic, and some patches may not match the file's exact style. * **Online access**: some fixes may require online access, even if their parent audit doesn't. For example, [unpinned-uses](./audits.md#unpinned-uses) doesn't require online access to _detect_ unpinned uses, but it does require online access (and a GitHub token) to fetch the latest commit SHA for pinning. ## Filtering results There are two straightforward ways to filter `zizmor`'s results: 1. If all you need is severity or confidence filtering (e.g. "I want only medium-severity and/or medium-confidence and above results"), then you can use the `--min-severity` and `--min-confidence` flags: !!! tip `--min-severity` and `--min-confidence` are available in `v0.6.0` and later. !!! warning "Deprecation" `--min-severity=unknown` and `--min-confidence=unknown` are **deprecated** as of `v1.14.0` and will be removed in a future release. Users should omit these entirely, as they were no-ops even prior to deprecation. ```bash # filter informational, and low findings with low confidence zizmor --min-severity=medium --min-confidence=medium ... ``` 2. If you need more advanced filtering (with nontrivial conditions or state considerations), then consider using `--format=json` and using `jq` (or a script) to perform your filtering. As a starting point, here's how you can use `jq` to filter `zizmor`'s JSON output to only results that are marked as "high confidence": ```bash zizmor --format=json-v1 ... | jq 'map(select(.determinations.confidence == "High"))' ``` ## Ignoring results `zizmor`'s defaults are not always 100% right for every possible use case. If you find that `zizmor` produces findings that aren't right for you (and **aren't** false positives, which should be reported!), then you can choose to *selectively ignore* results via either special ignore comments *or* a `zizmor.yml` configuration file. ### With comments !!! note Ignore comment support was added in `v0.6.0`. Findings can be ignored inline with `# zizmor: ignore[rulename]` comments. This is ideal for one-off ignores, where a whole `zizmor.yml` configuration file would be too heavyweight. Multiple different audits can be ignored with a single comment by separating each rule with a comma, e.g. `# zizmor: ignore[artipacked,ref-confusion]`. To ignore a single `template-injection` finding: ```yaml title="example.yml" run: | # zizmor: ignore[template-injection] echo "${{ github.event.issue.title }}" ``` Ignore comments can also have a trailing explanation: ```yaml title="example.yml" run: | # zizmor: ignore[template-injection] i promise this is safe echo "${{ github.event.issue.title }}" ``` !!! important An ignore comment can be placed anywhere in any span identified by a finding, **so long** as it can be identified as a YAML comment. In particular, this means that you **can't** place an ignore comment in the middle of a string or a block literal. For example, the following does not work: ```yaml title="example.yml" # this is not suppressed, since the comment is actually part of the string run: | echo "${{ github.event.issue.title }}" # zizmor: ignore[template-injection] ``` To fix this, you should place the ignore comment outside of the string, e.g. directly above it: ```yaml title="example.yml" run: | # zizmor: ignore[template-injection] echo "${{ github.event.issue.title }}" ``` ### With `zizmor.yml` When ignoring multiple findings (or entire files), a `zizmor.yml` configuration file is easier to maintain than one-off comments. Here's what a `zizmor.yml` file might look like: ```yaml title="zizmor.yml" rules: template-injection: ignore: - safe.yml - somewhat-safe.yml:123 - one-exact-spot.yml:123:456 ``` Concretely, this `zizmor.yml` configuration declares three ignore rules, all for the [`template-injection`](./audits.md#template-injection) audit: 1. Ignore all findings in `safe.yml`, regardless of line/column location 2. Ignore *any* findings in `somewhat-safe.yml` that occur on line 123 3. Ignore *one* finding in `one-exact-spot.yml` that occurs on line 123, column 456 More generally, the filename ignore syntax is `workflow.yml:line:col`, where `line` and `col` are both optional and 1-based (meaning `foo.yml:1:1` is the start of the file, not `foo.yml:0:0`). To pass a configuration to `zizmor`, you can either place `zizmor.yml` somewhere where `zizmor` [will discover it], or pass it explicitly via the `--config` argument. With `--config`, the file can be named anything: ```bash zizmor --config my-zizmor-config.yml /dir/to/audit ``` !!! important When using `--config`, only a single configuration file is used (instead of potentially discovering multiple configuration files, one per input source). As a result, using `--config` is **generally not recommended** unless auditing a single input source (file, directory, or remote repository). !!! tip Starting with `v1.8.0`, you can use the `ZIZMOR_CONFIG` environment variable to specify a configuration file. `ZIZMOR_CONFIG=my-config.yml` is equivalent to `--config my-config.yml`. [will discover it]: ./configuration.md#discovery See [Configuration: `rules..ignore`](./configuration.md#rulesidignore) for more details on writing ignore rules. ### Disabling ignores !!! tip `--no-ignores` is available in `v1.25.0` and later. Sometimes it's useful to disable ignores entirely. For example, if you're reviewing a repository that someone else has previously triaged with `zizmor`, you may want to temporarily disable their ignore rules to get a more complete picture of the repository's security posture. To do this, you can pass `--no-ignores` during audits: ```bash zizmor --no-ignores example/example ``` ## Caching between runs !!! tip Persistent caching (between runs of `zizmor`) is available in `v0.10.0` and later. !!! warning Caches can contain sensitive metadata, especially when auditing private repositories! Think twice before sharing your cache or reusing it across machine/visibility boundaries. `zizmor` caches HTTP responses from GitHub's REST APIs to speed up individual audits. This HTTP cache is persisted and re-used between runs as well. By default `zizmor` will cache to an appropriate user-level caching directory: * Linux and macOS: `$XDG_CACHE_DIR` (`~/.cache/zizmor` by default) * Windows: `~\AppData\Roaming\woodruffw\zizmor`. To override the default caching directory, pass `--cache-dir`: ```bash # cache in /tmp instead zizmor --cache-dir /tmp/zizmor ... ``` ## Other GitHub hosts !!! warning Support for custom GitHub Enterprise instances is provided on a **best-effort** basis. If you're a corporate user of `zizmor` who is interested in improving `zizmor`'s GitHub Enterprise support, please [let us know](https://github.com/zizmorcore/zizmor/issues/new) and [consider sponsoring](./index.md#sponsoring) development in this area! `zizmor` supports GitHub instances other than `github.com`. To use it with your [GitHub Enterprise](https://github.com/enterprise) instance (either cloud or self-hosted), pass your instance's domain with `--gh-hostname` or `GH_HOST`: ```bash zizmor --gh-hostname custom.example.com ... # or, with GH_HOST GH_HOST=custom.ghe.com zizmor ... ``` ## Limitations `zizmor` can help you write more secure GitHub workflow and action definitions, as well as help you find exploitable bugs in existing definitions. However, like all tools, `zizmor` is **not a panacea**, and has fundamental limitations that must be kept in mind. This page documents some of those limitations. ### `zizmor` is a _static_ analysis tool { #static-analysis } `zizmor` is a _static_ analysis tool. It never executes any code, nor does it have access to any runtime state. In contrast, GitHub Actions workflow and action definitions are highly dynamic, and can be influenced by inputs that can only be inspected at runtime. For example, here is a workflow where a job's matrix is generated at runtime by a previous job, making the matrix impossible to analyze statically: ```yaml build-matrix: name: Build the matrix runs-on: ubuntu-latest outputs: matrix: ${{ steps.set-matrix.outputs.matrix }} steps: - id: set-matrix run: | echo "matrix=$(python generate_matrix.py)" >> "${GITHUB_OUTPUT}" run: name: ${{ matrix.name }} needs: - build-matrix runs-on: ubuntu-latest strategy: matrix: ${{ fromJson(needs.build-matrix.outputs.matrix) }} steps: - run: | echo "hello ${{ matrix.something }}" ``` In the above, the expansion of `${{ matrix.something }}` is entirely controlled by the output of `generate_matrix.py`, which is only known at runtime. In such cases, `zizmor` will err on the side of verbosity. For example, the [template-injection](./audits.md#template-injection) audit will flag `${{ matrix.something }}` as a potential code injection risk, since it can't infer anything about what `matrix.something` might expand to. ### `zizmor` audits workflow and action _definitions_ only { #definitions-only } `zizmor` audits workflow and action _definitions_ only. That means the contents of `foo.yml` (for your workflow definitions) or `action.yml` (for your composite or Docker action definitions). In practice, this means that `zizmor` does **not** analyze other files referenced by workflow and action definitions. For example: ```yaml example: runs-on: ubuntu-latest steps: - name: step-1 run: | echo foo=$(bar) >> $GITHUB_ENV - name: step-2 run: | # some-script.sh contains the same code as step-1 ./some-script.sh ``` `zizmor` can analyze `step-1` above, because the code it executes is present within the workflow definition itself. It *cannot* analyze `step-2` beyond the presence of a script execution, since it doesn't audit shell scripts or any other kind of files. More generally, `zizmor` cannot analyze files indirectly referenced within workflow/action definitions, as they may not actually exist until runtime. For example, `some-script.sh` above may have been generated or downloaded outside of any repository-tracked state. ### YAML anchors { #yaml-anchors } !!! warning "Beta" `zizmor`'s support for YAML anchors is currently in **beta**. If you encounter a problem, please [file a bug report](https://github.com/zizmorcore/zizmor/issues/new). `zizmor` tries very hard to present *useful* source spans in its audit results. To do this, `zizmor` needs to know a lot of about the inner workings of the YAML serialization format that GitHub Actions workflows, action definitions, and Dependabot files are expressed in. YAML is a complicated serialization format, but GitHub *mostly* uses a tractable subset of it. One conspicuous exception to this is [YAML anchors](https://yaml.org/spec/1.2.2/#3222-anchors-and-aliases), which GitHub has [decided to support](https://github.blog/changelog/2025-09-18-actions-yaml-anchors-and-non-public-workflow-templates/) in workflow and action definitions as of September 2025. Anchors make `zizmor`'s analysis job *much* harder, as they introduce a layer of (arbitrarily deep) indirection and misalignment between the deserialized object model (which is what `zizmor` analyzes) and the source representation (which `zizmor` spans back to). If you're having issues with inputs containing anchors, see [Troubleshooting - YAML anchors]. [Troubleshooting - YAML anchors]: ./troubleshooting.md#yaml-anchors "}

# Audit Rules

This page documents each of the audits currently implemented in `zizmor`.

See each audit's section for its scope, behavior, and other information.

Legend:

## `anonymous-definition`

| Type            | Examples         | Introduced in | Works offline | Auto-fixes available | Configurable |
|-----------------|------------------|---------------|----------------|--------------------|--------------|
| Workflow, Action | N/A              | v1.10.0       | ✅             | ❌                 | ❌            |

Detects workflows or action definitions that lack a `name:` field.

GitHub explicitly allows workflows to omit the `name:` field, and allows (but
doesn't document) the same for action definitions. When `name:` is omitted, the
workflow or action is rendered anonymously in the GitHub Actions UI, making it
harder to understand which definition is running.

!!! note

    This is a `--pedantic` only audit, due to a lack of security impact.

### Remediation

Add a `name:` field to your workflow or action.

=== "Before :warning:"

    ```yaml title="anonymous-definition.yml"
    on: push

    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: echo "Hello!"
    ```

=== "After :white_check_mark:"

    ```yaml title="anonymous-definition.yml" hl_lines="1"
    name: Echo Test
    on: push

    jobs:
      build:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - run: echo "Hello!"
    ```

## `archived-uses`

| Type     | Examples         | Introduced in | Works offline  | Auto-fixes available | Configurable |
|----------|------------------|---------------|----------------|--------------------|--------------|
| Workflow, Action | [archived-uses.yml] | v1.19.0        | ✅             | ❌                 | ❌           |

[archived-uses.yml]: https://github.com/zizmorcore/zizmor/blob/main/crates/zizmor/tests/integration/test-data/archived-uses.yml


Detects `#!yaml uses:` clauses that reference [archived repositories].

[archived repositories]: https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/archiving-a-github-repository/archiving-repositories

Archival on GitHub makes a repository read-only, and indicates that the
repository is no longer maintained. Using actions or reusable workflows from archived
represents a supply chain risk:

- Unmaintained repositories are more likely to accumulate indirect vulnerabilties,
  including in any dependencies that have been vendored into JavaScript actions
  (or that are used indirectly through transitive dependencies that have gone
  stale).

- Any vulnerabilities discovered in the action or reusable workflow *itself*
  are unlikely to be fixed, since the repository is read-only.
  
Consequently, users are encouraged to avoid dependening on archived repositories
for actions or reusable workflows.

### Remediation

Depending on the archived repository's functionality, you may be able to:

- _Remove_ the action/reusable workflow entirely. Actions @actions-rs/cargo,
  for example, can be replaced by directly invoking the correct `#!bash cargo ...`
  command in a `#!yaml run:` step.
  
- _Replace_ the archived action/reusable workflow with a maintained alternative.
  For example, @actions/setup-ruby can be replaced with @ruby/setup-ruby.
  
!!! tip

    Many archived actions are thin wrappers around GitHub's REST and GraphQL
    APIs. In most cases, you can replace these actions with usage of the
    [`gh` CLI](https://cli.github.com/), which is pre-installed on GitHub-hosted
    runners.
    
    For more information, see [Using GitHub CLI in workflows].
    
    [Using GitHub CLI in workflows]: https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/write-workflows/choose-what-workflows-do/use-github-cli

[artipacked.yml]: https://github.com/woodruffw/gha-hazmat/blob/main/.github/workflows/artipacked.yml

Detects local filesystem `git` credential storage on GitHub Actions, as well as
potential avenues for unintentional persistence of credentials in artifacts.

By default, using @actions/checkout causes a credential to be persisted on disk.
Versions below v6.0.0 store the credential directly in the checked-out repo's
`.git/config`, while v6.0.0 and later store it under `$RUNNER_TEMP`.

Subsequent steps may accidentally publicly persist the credential, e.g. by
including it in a publicly accessible artifact via @actions/upload-artifact.

However, even without this, persisting the credential on disk is non-ideal
unless actually needed.

!!! note "Behavior change"

    Starting with zizmor v1.17.0, this audit produces lower-severity findings
    when v6.0.0 or higher of @actions/checkout is used. This reflects a
    change in v6.0.0's credential persistence behavior towards a more
    misuse-resistant location.
    
    See orgs/community?179107 for additional information.

Other resources:

* [ArtiPACKED: Hacking Giants Through a Race Condition in GitHub Actions Artifacts]

### Remediation

Unless needed for `git` operations, @actions/checkout should be used with
`#!yaml persist-credentials: false`.

If the persisted credential is needed, it should be made explicit
with `#!yaml persist-credentials: true`.

=== "Before :warning:"

    ```yaml title="artipacked.yml" hl_lines="7"
    on: push

    jobs:
      artipacked:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 # v4.2.2
    ```

=== "After :white_check_mark:"

    ```yaml title="artipacked.yml" hl_lines="7-9"
    on: push

    jobs:
      artipacked:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@11bd71901bbe5b1630ceea73d27597364c9af683 # v4.2.2
            with:
              persist-credentials: false
    ```


## `bot-conditions`

| Type     | Examples                | Introduced in | Works offline  | Auto-fixes available | Configurable |
|----------|-------------------------|---------------|----------------|--------------------| ---------------|
| Workflow  | [bot-conditions.yml]   | v1.2.0      | ✅             | ✅                 | ❌  |

[bot-conditions.yml]: https://github.com/woodruffw/gha-hazmat/blob/main/.github/workflows/bot-conditions.yml

Detects potentially spoofable bot conditions.

Many workflows allow trustworthy bots (such as [Dependabot](https://github.com/dependabot))
to bypass checks or otherwise perform privileged actions. This is often done
with a `github.actor` check, e.g.:

```yaml
if: github.actor == 'dependabot[bot]'
```

However, this condition is spoofable: `github.actor` refers to the *last* actor
to perform an "action" on the triggering context, and not necessarily
the actor actually causing the trigger. An attacker can take
advantage of this discrepancy to create a PR where the `HEAD` commit
has `github.actor == 'dependabot[bot]'` but the rest of the branch history
contains attacker-controlled code, bypassing the actor check.

Other resources:

* [GitHub Actions exploitations: Dependabot]

### Remediation

In general, checking a trigger's authenticity via `github.actor` is
insufficient. Instead, most users should use `github.event.pull_request.user.login`
or similar, since that context refers to the actor that *created* the Pull Request
rather than the last one to modify it.

More generally,
[GitHub's documentation recommends](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/dependabot/working-with-dependabot/automating-dependabot-with-github-actions)
not using `pull_request_target` for auto-merge workflows.

!!! example

    === "Before :warning:"

        ```yaml title="bot-conditions.yml" hl_lines="1 6"
        on: pull_request_target

        jobs:
          automerge:
            runs-on: ubuntu-latest
            if: github.actor == 'dependabot[bot]' && github.repository == github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name
            steps:
              - run: gh pr merge --auto --merge "$PR_URL"
                env:
                  PR_URL: ${{ github.event.pull_request.html_url }}
                  GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        ```

    === "After :white_check_mark:"
"}

## Operating Modes

`zizmor` has three *operating modes*:

* **Offline**: `zizmor` will not access the Internet,
  will not fetch remote repositories, and will not perform
  any audits that require online access (e.g. to the GitHub API).
* **Online**: `zizmor` will fetch remote repositories
  as necessary, and will perform all audits that require
  online access.
* **Online sans audits**: `zizmor` will fetch remote repositories
  as necessary, but will skip any audits that require online access.

`zizmor` attempts to select a default operating mode based on the user's
environment:

- If `ZIZMOR_OFFLINE` is set, then `zizmor` runs in offline mode.
- If `GH_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN` or `ZIZMOR_GITHUB_TOKEN` is set, then `zizmor` runs in online mode with audits.
    - Additionally `ZIZMOR_NO_ONLINE_AUDITS` is set, then `zizmor` runs
      online sans audits.
- If neither `ZIZMOR_OFFLINE` nor `GH_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_TOKEN`/`ZIZMOR_GITHUB_TOKEN` are set, then `zizmor` runs
  in offline mode.

Or, as a flowchart:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  B{ZIZMOR_OFFLINE set?} -- Yes --> C[Offline mode]
  B -- No --> D{GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN/ZIZMOR_GITHUB_TOKEN set?}
  D -- No --> C
  D -- Yes --> E{ZIZMOR_NO_ONLINE_AUDITS set?}
  E -- Yes --> F[Online sans audits mode]
  E -- No --> G[Online mode]
```

Each operating mode can also be made explicit through command-line flags:

```bash
# force offline, even if GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN/ZIZMOR_GITHUB_TOKEN is present
# this disables all online actions, including repository fetches
zizmor --offline workflow.yml

# passing a token explicitly will enable online mode
# in this case, we use the `gh` CLI token
zizmor --gh-token $(gh auth token) workflow.yml

# online for the purpose of fetching the input (example/example),
# but all audits themselves are offline
zizmor --no-online-audits --gh-token $(gh auth token) example/example
```

### GitHub API token permissions

!!! tip

    If you're running `zizmor` locally with an online mode, it is
    **strongly recommended** that you use `gh auth token` from the [GitHub CLI]
    to automatically access an API token and avoid error-prone manual
    provisioning.

    This token is almost always pre-configured with sufficient permissions,
    meaning that you **do not** need any of the manual steps below.

    [GitHub CLI]: https://cli.github.com/

When running in an online mode, `zizmor` uses the GitHub API for
various operations, including fetching a repository's contents
(for the collection phase) and fetching tag/branch/commit histories
(for the auditing phase).

Generally speaking, `zizmor` does **not** require any special permissions
from its GitHub API token: it uses the token *primarily* to provide
authentication for rate-limited API requests.

However, if you are auditing a private remote repository (e.g.
`zizmor myorg/private-repo`) or auditing _any_ input that contains
private references (e.g. `#!yaml uses: myorg/private-action`), then
you may need to provision permissions for the token:

- `#!yaml contents: read` for GitHub Actions
- `repo` for OAuth tokens and "classic" PATs
- An appropriate repository access scope for fine-grained PATs

In addition to these permissions, some integrations of `zizmor`
(like GitHub Advanced Security) may require additional permissions
in the context of GitHub Actions. See
[Integration - GitHub Actions](./integrations.md#github-actions) for more details.

## Output formats

`zizmor` always produces output on `stdout`.

### Cargo-style output ("plain")

By default, `zizmor` produces `cargo`-style diagnostic output.

```console
error[template-injection]: code injection via template expansion
  --> ./tests/integration/test-data/template-injection/pr-425-backstop/action.yml:31:56
   |
29 |       uses: azure/powershell@whatever
   |       ------------------------------- action accepts arbitrary code
30 |       with:
31 |         inlineScript: Get-AzVM -ResourceGroupName "${{ inputs.expandme }}"
   |         ------------ via this input                    ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ may expand into attacker-controllable code
   |
   = note: audit confidence → High
```

This output will be colorized by default when sent to a supporting terminal and
uncolorized by default when piped to another program. Users can also explicitly
disable output colorization by setting `NO_COLOR=1` in their environment.

This format can also be explicitly selected with `--format=plain`.

#### Audit documentation links

By default, `zizmor` includes links to relevant documentation pages
for each finding in its plain output format. These links are provided via
[OSC 8](https://gist.github.com/egmontkob/eb114294efbcd5adb1944c9f3cb5feda)
hyperlinks, which are supported by many modern terminal emulators.

For example, in the output above, `template-injection` within
`error[template-injection]: ...` is a clickable link that takes you to
the [template-injection](./audits#template-injection) audit documentation.

In addition to these OSC 8 links, `zizmor` also includes the full URL
as part of each finding _if_ it detects a non-terminal output _or_
a CI environment (e.g. GitHub Actions).

To make this behavior explicir, users can supply the `--show-audit-urls`
option:

```bash
# always show audit documentation URLs, even if output is to a terminal
zizmor --show-audit-urls=always ...

# never show audit documentation URLs
zizmor --show-audit-urls=never ... 
```

!!! note

    `--show-audit-urls=...` is available in `v1.19.0` and later.

#### Color customization

When invoked from a terminal, `zizmor` will attempt to enrich its output
with ANSI colors.

!!! note

    `--color` is available in `v1.5.0` and later.

Some users may prefer to explicitly enable or disable this behavior. For
example, GitHub Actions is not a terminal but it does support ANSI colors,
so enabling colors in GitHub Actions can make logs more readable.

To explicitly control `zizmor`'s colorization behavior, use the
`--color` option:

```bash
# force colorization
zizmor --color=always ...

# force no colorization
zizmor --color=never ...
```

`zizmor` also respects various environment variables for colorization:

* [`NO_COLOR`](https://no-color.org/): if set to any value, disables colorization
* [`FORCE_COLOR`](https://force-color.org/): if set to any value, enables colorization
* [`CLICOLOR_FORCE`](https://bixense.com/clicolors/): if set to any value, enables colorization

const p = "*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /workspace/anonymous_definition.py
+"""Small source-aware implementation of zizmor's anonymous-definition audit."""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import os
+import re
+
+
+def _offset(text: str, row: int, col: int = 0) -> int:
+    lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
+    return len("".join(lines[:row]).encode("utf-8")) + len(lines[row][:col].encode("utf-8")) if row < len(lines) else len(text.encode("utf-8"))
+
+
+def _point(text: str, offset: int) -> dict:
+    raw = text.encode("utf-8")[:offset]
+    row = raw.count(b"\n")
+    col = len(raw.rsplit(b"\n", 1)[-1])
+    return {"row": row, "column": col}
+
+
+def _finding(text: str, filename: str, annotation: str, route: list, feature_kind: str,
+             kind: str, start: int, end: int, feature: str, severity: str) -> dict:
+    path = os.path.abspath(filename)
+    return {
+        "ident": "anonymous-definition",
+        "desc": "workflow or action definition without a name",
+        "url": "https://docs.zizmor.sh/audits/#anonymous-definition",
+        "determinations": {"confidence": "High", "severity": severity, "persona": "Pedantic"},
+        "locations": [{
+            "symbolic": {"key": {"Local": {"prefix": None, "given_path": path}},
+                         "annotation": annotation,
+                         "route": {"route": [{"Key": str(part)} for part in route]},
+                         "feature_kind": feature_kind, "kind": kind},
+            "concrete": {"location": {"start_point": _point(text, start),
+                                          "end_point": _point(text, end),
+                                          "offset_span": {"start": start, "end": end}},
+                         "feature": feature, "comments": []},
+        }],
+        "ignored": False,
+    }
+
+
+def audit_anonymous_definition(text: str, filename: str, persona: str = "pedantic") -> list[dict]:
+    """Return anonymous workflow/job findings for a workflow source string.
+
+    This rule is pedantic-only. The caller should invoke it when that persona
+    is enabled; the check here also accepts the persona for convenient use.
+    """
+    if str(persona).lower() not in ("pedantic", "auditor"):
+        return []
+    lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
+    if not lines:
+        return []
+    # This module targets workflows. Actions are recognized by a runs mapping
+    # and are intentionally left to callers that know the collected input kind.
+    if not any(re.match(r"^jobs\s*:", line) for line in lines):
+        return []
+    findings = []
+    if not any(re.match(r"^name\s*:", line) for line in lines):
+        start, end = 0, len(text.encode("utf-8"))
+        findings.append(_finding(text, filename, "this workflow", [], "Normal", "Primary",
+                                 start, end, text, "Low"))
+    in_jobs = False
+    jobs_indent = 0
+    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
+        body = line.rstrip("\r\n")
+        indent = len(body) - len(body.lstrip(" "))
+        if indent == 0:
+            in_jobs = bool(re.match(r"^jobs\s*:", body))
+            jobs_indent = indent
+            continue
+        if not in_jobs or not body.strip() or body.lstrip().startswith("#"):
+            continue
+        if indent <= jobs_indent:
+            in_jobs = False
+            continue
+        # A job key has exactly one indentation level below `jobs:`.
+        if indent != jobs_indent + 2:
+            continue
+        m = re.match(r"^\s*([^#][^:]*?)\s*:\s*(?:#.*)?$", body)
+        if not m:
+            continue
+        job = m.group(1).strip().strip("'\"")
+        next_has_name = False
+        for later in lines[i + 1:]:
+            lb = later.rstrip("\r\n")
+            if lb.strip() and not lb.lstrip().startswith("#"):
+                li = len(lb) - len(lb.lstrip(" "))
+                if li <= indent:
+                    break
+                if re.match(r"^\s+name\s*:", lb):
+                    next_has_name = True
+                    break
+        if next_has_name:
+            continue
+        key_start_char = len(body) - len(body.lstrip(" "))
+        token = m.group(1).strip()
+        # Locate just the YAML key, excluding quotes when present.
+        token_char = body.find(token, key_start_char)
+        if token.startswith(("'", '"')) and token[-1:] == token[:1]:
+            token_char += 1
+            token = token[1:-1]
+        start = _offset(text, i, token_char)
+        end = start + len(token.encode("utf-8"))
+        findings.append(_finding(text, filename, "this job", ["jobs", job], "KeyOnly",
+                                 "Primary", start, end, token, "Informational"))
+    return findings
+
*** End Patch";
text(await tools.apply_patch(p));

+"""Output encoders shared by the CLI and audit modules."""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import os
+
+
+def _escape_property(value: object) -> str:
+    # GitHub workflow command properties escape %, CR, LF, ':' and ','.
+    value = str(value)
+    return (value.replace("%", "%25").replace("\r", "%0D").replace("\n", "%0A")
+            .replace(":", "%3A").replace(",", "%2C"))
+
+
+def _escape_data(value: object) -> str:
+    return str(value).replace("%", "%25").replace("\r", "%0D").replace("\n", "%0A")
+
+
+def format_github(findings: list[dict]) -> str:
+    """Render JSON-v1 findings as GitHub Actions workflow commands."""
+    out: list[str] = []
+    for item in findings:
+        det = item.get("determinations", {})
+        severity = str(det.get("severity", "")).lower()
+        level = "error" if severity == "high" else "warning"
+        locations = item.get("locations") or []
+        primary = next((loc for loc in locations
+                        if loc.get("symbolic", {}).get("kind") == "Primary"),
+                       locations[0] if locations else {})
+        symbolic = primary.get("symbolic", {})
+        concrete = primary.get("concrete", {})
+        key = symbolic.get("key", {})
+        local = key.get("Local", {}) if isinstance(key, dict) else {}
+        path = local.get("given_path", "")
+        line = concrete.get("location", {}).get("start_point", {}).get("row", 0) + 1
+        display = os.path.basename(path) if path and path != "<stdin>" else path
+        annotation = symbolic.get("annotation", "")
+        desc = item.get("desc", "")
+        message = f"{display}:{line}: {desc}: {annotation}" if display else f"{desc}: {annotation}"
+        props = [f"file={_escape_property(path)}", f"line={line}",
+                 f"title={_escape_property(item.get('ident', ''))}"]
+        out.append(f"::{level} {','.join(props)}::{_escape_data(message)}")
+    return "\n".join(out) + ("\n" if out else "")
+
*** End Patch";

{"chunk_id":"ebf86a","wall_time_seconds":0.009603571,"exit_code":0,"original_token_count":665,"output":""""Helpers for building zizmor's JSON v1 finding representation.

Audit modules can use ``location`` and ``finding`` rather than duplicating the
wire format. Source offsets and rows are zero based, as in the reference JSON.
"""

from __future__ import annotations


def source_location(text: str, start: int, end: int) -> dict:
    """Return the concrete location for the half-open source byte/char range."""
    start = max(0, min(len(text), start))
    end = max(start, min(len(text), end))
    before = text[:start]
    until = text[:end]
    sr, er = before.count("\n"), until.count("\n")
    sc = len(before.rsplit("\n", 1)[-1].encode("utf-8"))
    ec = len(until.rsplit("\n", 1)[-1].encode("utf-8"))
    return {
        "location": {
            "start_point": {"row": sr, "column": sc},
            "end_point": {"row": er, "column": ec},
            "offset_span": {"start": len(before.encode("utf-8")),
                            "end": len(until.encode("utf-8"))},
        },
        "feature": text[start:end],
        "comments": [],
    }


def finding_location(path: str, annotation: str, route: list, text: str,
                     start: int, end: int, *, kind: str = "Primary",
                     feature_kind: str = "Normal", prefix=None) -> dict:
    """Build one JSON-v1 location from route components and a source span."""
    components = [{"Key": part} if isinstance(part, str) else {"Index": part}
                  for part in route]
    return {
        "symbolic": {
            "key": {"Local": {"prefix": prefix, "given_path": path}},
            "annotation": annotation,
            "route": {"route": components},
            "feature_kind": feature_kind,
            "kind": kind,
        },
        "concrete": source_location(text, start, end),
    }


def finding(ident: str, desc: str, severity: str, confidence: str,
            persona: str, locations: list, *, ignored: bool = False) -> dict:
    """Build one JSON-v1 finding. Values use title case (e.g. ``High``)."""
    return {
        "ident": ident,
        "desc": desc,
        "url": f"https://docs.zizmor.sh/audits/#{ident}",
        "determinations": {
            "confidence": confidence,
            "severity": severity,
            "persona": persona,
        },
        "locations": locations,
        "ignored": ignored,
    }

{"chunk_id":"58ee20","wall_time_seconds":0.000004081,"exit_code":0,"original_token_count":3576,"output":""""Offline `unpinned-uses` audit helper for GitHub Actions YAML."""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import re


_SHA = re.compile(r"^[0-9a-fA-F]{40}$")
_USES = re.compile(r"^(\s*)-?\s*uses\s*:\s*(.*?)\s*(?:#.*)?$")


def _route_key(key: str) -> dict:
    return {"Key": key}


def audit_uses(text: str, filename: str, persona: str = "regular") -> list[dict]:
    """Return unpinned-uses findings in zizmor's JSON-v1 finding shape.

    This deliberately handles the common workflow step and reusable-workflow
    forms without requiring a third-party YAML parser.
    """
    absolute = os.path.abspath(filename)
    lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
    findings: list[dict] = []
    job = None
    in_jobs = False
    in_runs = False
    in_steps = False
    step = -1
    indent_jobs = indent_steps = -1
    byte_offset = 0
    for row, raw in enumerate(lines):
        line = raw.rstrip("\r\n")
        stripped = line.strip()
        indent = len(line) - len(line.lstrip())
        if not stripped or stripped.startswith("#"):
            byte_offset += len(raw.encode("utf-8"))
            continue
        if indent == 0:
            in_jobs = stripped == "jobs:"
            in_runs = stripped == "runs:"
            indent_jobs = indent if in_jobs else -1
            in_steps = False
            job = None
        elif in_jobs and indent == 2 and stripped.endswith(":") and not stripped.startswith(("-", "#")):
            job = stripped[:-1].strip("'\"")
            in_steps = False
            step = -1
        elif ((job is not None and indent == 4) or (in_runs and indent == 2)) and stripped == "steps:":
            in_steps = True
            indent_steps = indent
            step = -1
        elif in_steps and indent <= indent_steps:
            in_steps = False

        if in_steps and stripped.startswith("-"):
            step += 1

        match = _USES.match(line)
        if match:
            value = match.group(2).strip().strip("'\"")
            docker = value.startswith("docker://")
            # Docker actions without an explicit tag or digest resolve to
            # `latest`; Docker refs with a tag or digest are accepted here.
            docker_unpinned = docker and ":" not in value[len("docker://"):].rsplit("/", 1)[-1] and "@" not in value
            if value and not value.startswith(("./", "../")) and (docker_unpinned or not docker):
                ref = value.rsplit("@", 1)[1] if "@" in value else ""
                if docker_unpinned or not _SHA.fullmatch(ref):
                    colon = line.find(":")
                    value_at = colon + 1
                    while value_at < len(line) and line[value_at].isspace():
                        value_at += 1
                    # YAML `- uses:` puts the key after the list marker; the
                    # source span is always the scalar itself.
                    start = byte_offset + len(line[:value_at].encode("utf-8"))
                    end = start + len(value.encode("utf-8"))
                    if in_steps and job is not None:
                        route = [_route_key("jobs"), _route_key(job), _route_key("steps"), {"Index": max(step, 0)}, _route_key("uses")]
                    elif in_steps and in_runs:
                        route = [_route_key("runs"), _route_key("steps"), {"Index": max(step, 0)}, _route_key("uses")]
                    elif job is not None:
                        route = [_route_key("jobs"), _route_key(job), _route_key("uses")]
                    else:
                        route = [_route_key("runs"), _route_key("steps"), {"Index": 0}, _route_key("uses")]
                    location = {
                        "start_point": {"row": row, "column": len(line[:value_at].encode("utf-8"))},
                        "end_point": {"row": row, "column": len(line[:value_at].encode("utf-8")) + len(value.encode("utf-8"))},
                        "offset_span": {"start": start, "end": end},
                    }
                    severity = "Medium" if docker else "High"
                    annotation = "image is not pinned to a tag, branch, or hash ref" if docker else "action is not pinned to a hash (required by blanket policy)"
                    feature = value if not docker else value[len("docker://"):]
                    findings.append({
                        "ident": "unpinned-uses",
                        "desc": "unpinned action reference",
                        "url": "https://docs.zizmor.sh/audits/#unpinned-uses",
                        "determinations": {"confidence": "High", "severity": severity, "persona": persona.capitalize()},
                        "locations": [{
                            "symbolic": {
                                "key": {"Local": {"prefix": None, "given_path": absolute}},
                                "annotation": annotation,
                                "route": {"route": route},
                                "feature_kind": {"Subfeature": {"after": 0, "fragment": {"Raw": feature}}},
                                "kind": "Primary",
                            },
                            "concrete": {"location": location, "feature": value, "comments": []},
                        }],
                        "ignored": False,
                    })
        byte_offset += len(raw.encode("utf-8"))
    return findings

"""Small source-based implementation of zizmor's bot-conditions audit.

The function returns JSON-v1-shaped findings so it can be used by the main
auditor without requiring a YAML library.
"""
import re
from finding import finding, finding_location

PATTERN = re.compile(r"github\.(actor|triggering_actor)\s+==\s+'([^']*\[bot\])'", re.I)


def audit_bot_conditions(source: str, filename: str, persona: str = "Regular"):
    lines = source.splitlines(keepends=True)
    starts = []
    off = 0
    for line in lines:
        starts.append(off)
        off += len(line)

    found = []
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        m = re.search(r"^\s*if:\s*(.*)$", line.rstrip("\r\n"))
        if not m:
            continue
        value = m.group(1)
        match = PATTERN.search(value)
        if not match:
            continue
        # Infer the nearest enclosing job from YAML indentation.
        if_indent = len(line) - len(line.lstrip())
        job_i = None
        for j in range(i - 1, -1, -1):
            s = lines[j].rstrip("\r\n")
            ind = len(s) - len(s.lstrip())
            if ind < if_indent and re.match(r"^\s{2}[^\s#][^:]*:\s*(?:#.*)?$", s):
                job_i = j
                break
        if job_i is None:
            continue
        jobline = lines[job_i].rstrip("\r\n")
        job_indent = len(jobline) - len(jobline.lstrip())
        name_match = re.match(r"\s*([^:#][^:]*):", jobline)
        if not name_match:
            continue
        job = name_match.group(1).strip().strip("'\"")
        key_start = starts[job_i] + job_indent
        key_end = key_start + len(name_match.group(1).strip())
        expr = match.group(0)
        context = match.group(1)
        bot = re.escape(match.group(2))
        fragment_regex = rf"github\.{context}\s+==\s+'{bot}'"
        expr_start = starts[i] + m.start(1) + match.start()
        expr_end = expr_start + len(expr)
        locations = [
            finding_location(filename, "this job", ["jobs", job], source, key_start, key_end,
                             kind="Related", feature_kind="KeyOnly"),
            finding_location(filename, "actor context may be spoofable", ["jobs", job, "if"], source,
                             expr_start, expr_end, feature_kind={"Subfeature": {"after": 0, "fragment": {
                                 "Regex": fragment_regex}}}),
        ]
        found.append(finding("bot-conditions", "spoofable bot actor check", "High", "High", persona, locations))
    return found


"""A lightweight offline implementation of the excessive-permissions audit."""

from __future__ import annotations

import re

from finding import finding, finding_location


def audit_excessive_permissions(text: str, filename: str,
                               persona: str = "Regular") -> list[dict]:
    """Report jobs which inherit GitHub's broad default token permissions.

    This intentionally operates on source indentation so emitted spans point
    back to the original YAML, without requiring a non-standard YAML package.
    """
    lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
    offsets = []
    at = 0
    for line in lines:
        offsets.append(at)
        at += len(line)

    # Locate top-level `permissions:`. A key at the top level applies to all
    # jobs; per-job permission keys suppress findings for that job only.
    workflow_permissions = any(
        re.match(r"^permissions\s*:", line.rstrip("\r\n")) for line in lines
    )
    jobs_idx = next((i for i, line in enumerate(lines)
                     if re.match(r"^jobs\s*:", line.rstrip("\r\n"))), None)
    if workflow_permissions or jobs_idx is None:
        return []

    jobs_indent = len(lines[jobs_idx]) - len(lines[jobs_idx].lstrip(" "))
    found = []
    i = jobs_idx + 1
    while i < len(lines):
        raw = lines[i].rstrip("\r\n")
        stripped = raw.lstrip(" ")
        indent = len(raw) - len(stripped)
        if stripped and not stripped.startswith("#") and indent <= jobs_indent:
            break
        # Job IDs are immediate children of jobs. Permit quoted ids.
        m = re.match(r"^\s+([^#][^:]*):(?:\s*(?:#.*)?)?$", raw)
        if m and indent > jobs_indent:
            job_indent = indent
            start_line = i
            j = i + 1
            has_permissions = False
            while j < len(lines):
                r = lines[j].rstrip("\r\n")
                s = r.lstrip(" ")
                ind = len(r) - len(s)
                if s and not s.startswith("#") and ind <= job_indent:
                    break
                if re.match(r"^\s+permissions\s*:", r):
                    has_permissions = True
                j += 1
            if not has_permissions:
                # Match the job subtree, including its final line ending when
                # present; this is the span used by the reference diagnostic.
                end = offsets[j] if j < len(lines) else len(text)
                start = offsets[start_line]
                route = ["jobs", m.group(1).strip().strip("'\"")]
                loc_related = finding_location(
                    filename, "this job", route, text, start, end,
                    kind="Related")
                loc_primary = finding_location(
                    filename, "default permissions used due to no permissions: block",
                    route, text, start, end)
                # The symbolic feature is the whole job, while the concrete
                # node span begins at the job identifier scalar itself.
                key_start = start + len(lines[start_line]) - len(lines[start_line].lstrip(" "))
                key_column = key_start - offsets[start_line]
                for loc in (loc_related, loc_primary):
                    point = loc["concrete"]["location"]
                    point["start_point"] = {"row": start_line, "column": key_column}
                    point["offset_span"]["start"] = key_start
                found.append(finding(
                    "excessive-permissions", "overly broad permissions", "Medium",
                    "Medium", persona, [loc_related, loc_primary]))
            i = j
        else:
            i += 1
    return found
"""Offline insecure-commands audit."""
import re
from finding import finding, finding_location


def audit(text: str, filename: str, persona: str = "Regular") -> list[dict]:
    lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
    offsets = []
    pos = 0
    for line in lines:
        offsets.append(pos)
        pos += len(line)
    result = []
    # The variable is dangerous at workflow, job, and step scope. Associate
    # the location with its containing env mapping and construct a YAML route.
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        m = re.match(r"^(\s*)ACTIONS_ALLOW_UNSECURE_COMMANDS\s*:\s*(.*?)\s*(?:#.*)?(?:\r?\n)?$", line)
        if not m or m.group(2).strip(" '\" ").lower() not in ("true", "yes", "on"):
            continue
        indent = len(m.group(1))
        # Find the `env:` key that owns this value.
        env_i = i
        while env_i >= 0:
            em = re.match(r"^(\s*)env\s*:\s*(?:#.*)?(?:\r?\n)?$", lines[env_i])
            if em and len(em.group(1)) < indent:
                break
            env_i -= 1
        if env_i < 0:
            continue
        env_indent = len(re.match(r"^\s*", lines[env_i]).group())
        end_i = env_i + 1
        while end_i < len(lines):
            s = lines[end_i]
            if s.strip() and len(s) - len(s.lstrip()) <= env_indent:
                break
            end_i += 1
        route = []
        # Recover common GitHub Actions paths from indentation/key lines.
        for k in range(env_i - 1, -1, -1):
            jm = re.match(r"^\s{2}([\w-]+)\s*:\s*(?:#.*)?(?:\r?\n)?$", lines[k])
            if jm and re.match(r"^\s*jobs\s*:", lines[k-1] if k else ""):
                route = ["jobs", jm.group(1)]
                break
        if route:
            step_idx = 0
            for k in range(route and env_i - 1 or -1, -1, -1):
                if re.match(r"^\s{6}-\s", lines[k]):
                    step_idx = sum(1 for z in range(k + 1, env_i) if re.match(r"^\s{6}-\s", lines[z]))
                    route += ["steps", step_idx]
                    break
        route.append("env")
        start = offsets[env_i]
        end = offsets[end_i] if end_i < len(lines) else len(text)
        # YAML node spans stop before the newline that precedes the next
        # sibling; a final node includes the input's terminal newline.
        if end_i < len(lines) and end > start and text[end - 1:end] == "\n":
            end -= 1
        result.append(finding(
            "insecure-commands", "execution of insecure workflow commands is enabled",
            "High", "High", persona,
            [finding_location(filename, "insecure commands enabled here", route,
                              text, start, end)],
        ))
    return result
"}

def _escape_property(value: object) -> str:
    # GitHub workflow command properties escape %, CR, LF, ':' and ','.
    value = str(value)
    return (value.replace("%", "%25").replace("\r", "%0D").replace("\n", "%0A")
            .replace(":", "%3A").replace(",", "%2C"))


def _escape_data(value: object) -> str:
    return str(value).replace("%", "%25").replace("\r", "%0D").replace("\n", "%0A")


def format_github(findings: list[dict]) -> str:
    """Render JSON-v1 findings as GitHub Actions workflow commands."""
    out: list[str] = []
    for item in findings:
        det = item.get("determinations", {})
        severity = str(det.get("severity", "")).lower()
        level = "error" if severity == "high" else "notice" if severity == "informational" else "warning"
        locations = item.get("locations") or []
        primary = next((loc for loc in locations
                        if loc.get("symbolic", {}).get("kind") == "Primary"),
                       locations[0] if locations else {})
        symbolic = primary.get("symbolic", {})
        concrete = primary.get("concrete", {})
        key = symbolic.get("key", {})
        local = key.get("Local", {}) if isinstance(key, dict) else {}
        path = local.get("given_path", "")
        line = concrete.get("location", {}).get("start_point", {}).get("row", 0) + 1
        display = os.path.basename(path) if path and path != "<stdin>" else path
        annotation = symbolic.get("annotation", "")
        desc = item.get("desc", "")
        message = f"{display}:{line}: {desc}: {annotation}" if display else f"{desc}: {annotation}"
        props = [f"file={_escape_property(path)}", f"line={line}",
                 f"title={_escape_property(item.get('ident', ''))}"]
        out.append(f"::{level} {','.join(props)}::{_escape_data(message)}")
    return "\n".join(out) + ("\n" if out else "")


def format_sarif(findings: list[dict], version: str = "1.25.2") -> dict:
    """Convert JSON-v1 findings into the SARIF 2.1 structure used by zizmor."""
    rules = {}
    results = []

    def sarif_loc(loc):
        symbolic = loc.get("symbolic", {})
        concrete = loc.get("concrete", {})
        local = symbolic.get("key", {}).get("Local", {})
        path = local.get("given_path", "")
        point = concrete.get("location", {})
        start = point.get("start_point", {})
        end = point.get("end_point", {})
        region = {"startLine": start.get("row", 0) + 1,
                  "startColumn": start.get("column", 0) + 1,
                  "endLine": end.get("row", 0) + 1,
                  "endColumn": end.get("column", 0) + 1,
                  "sourceLanguage": "yaml",
                  "snippet": {"text": concrete.get("feature", "")}}
        return {"logicalLocations": [{"properties": {"symbolic": symbolic}}],
                "message": {"text": symbolic.get("annotation", "")},
                "physicalLocation": {"artifactLocation": {"uri": path}, "region": region}}

    for f in findings:
        ident, desc = f.get("ident", ""), f.get("desc", "")
        rid = f"zizmor/{ident}"
        url = f.get("url", "")
        rules[rid] = {"id": rid, "name": ident, "helpUri": url,
                      "help": {"text": desc, "markdown": f"`{ident}`: {desc}\n\nDocs: <{url}>"},
                      "properties": {"tags": ["security"]}}
        locations = f.get("locations", [])
        primary = next((x for x in locations if x.get("symbolic", {}).get("kind") == "Primary"),
                       locations[0] if locations else {})
        prim_sym = primary.get("symbolic", {})
        annotations = [sarif_loc(x) for x in locations]
        code_locs = []
        for loc in locations:
            item = sarif_loc(loc)
            item["importance"] = "essential" if loc.get("symbolic", {}).get("kind") == "Primary" else "important"
            code_locs.append({"location": item})
        det = f.get("determinations", {})
        sev = det.get("severity", "Medium").lower()
        level = "error" if sev == "high" else "warning" if sev in ("medium", "low") else "note"
        results.append({"ruleId": rid, "kind": "fail", "level": level,
                        "message": {"text": f"{desc}: {prim_sym.get('annotation', '')}"},
                        "locations": [sarif_loc(primary)] if primary else [],
                        "codeFlows": [{"threadFlows": [{"locations": code_locs}]}] if code_locs else [],
                        "properties": {"zizmor/confidence": det.get("confidence"),
                                       "zizmor/persona": det.get("persona"),
                                       "zizmor/severity": det.get("severity")}})
    return {"$schema": "https://docs.oasis-open.org/sarif/sarif/v2.1.0/os/schemas/sarif-schema-2.1.0.json",
            "version": "2.1.0",
            "runs": [{"invocations": [{"executionSuccessful": True}],
                      "results": results,
                      "tool": {"driver": {"name": "zizmor", "version": version,
                          "semanticVersion": version,
                          "informationUri": "https://docs.zizmor.sh",
                          "downloadUri": "https://github.com/zizmorcore/zizmor",
                          "rules": list(rules.values())}}}]}

            for result in current:

                    key = location.get("symbolic", {}).get("key", {})
                    if "Local" in key:
                        del key["Local"]
                        key["Stdin"] = {}
        results.extend(current)
    results.sort(key=lambda item: item.get("ident", ""))
    severities = ["informational", "low", "medium", "high"]
    confidences = ["low", "medium", "high"]
    if args.min_severity:
        threshold = severities.index(args.min_severity)
        results = [f for f in results if severities.index(f["determinations"]["severity"].lower()) >= threshold]
    if args.min_confidence:
        threshold = confidences.index(args.min_confidence)
        results = [f for f in results if confidences.index(f["determinations"]["confidence"].lower()) >= threshold]
    if args.format in ("json", "json-v1"):
        print(json.dumps(results, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
    elif args.format == "github":
        sys.stdout.write(format_github(results))
    elif args.format == "sarif":
        print(json.dumps(format_sarif(results, VERSION), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False))
    else:
        for f in results:
            print(f"error[{f['ident']}]: {f['desc']}")
            for loc in f["locations"]:
                p = loc["concrete"]["location"]["start_point"]
                name = loc["symbolic"]["key"]["Local"]["given_path"]
                print(f"  --> {name}:{p['row']+1}:{p['column']+1}")
                print(f"   = note: audit confidence → {f['determinations']['confidence']}")
    if args.no_exit_codes or args.format == "sarif" or not results:
        return 0
    rank = {"informational": 11, "low": 12, "medium": 13, "high": 14}
    return max(rank.get(f["determinations"]["severity"].lower(), 11) for f in results)

"""Offline implementation of common actions/checkout credential findings."""
import os
import re

from finding import finding, finding_location


def audit_artipacked(text: str, filename: str, persona: str = "Regular") -> list[dict]:
    lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
    starts, offset = [], 0
    for line in lines:
        starts.append(offset)
        offset += len(line.encode("utf-8"))
    out = []
    job = None
    in_steps = False
    step_idx = -1
    step_indent = -1
    i = 0
    while i < len(lines):
        raw = lines[i].rstrip("\r\n")
        indent = len(raw) - len(raw.lstrip(" "))
        stripped = raw.strip()
        if indent == 0:
            in_steps = False
            job = None
        if re.match(r"^jobs\s*:", raw):
            job = None
        elif re.match(r"^  [^\s#][^:]*:\s*(?:#.*)?$", raw):
            job = raw.strip().split(":", 1)[0].strip("'\"")
            in_steps = False
        elif job is not None and re.match(r"^\s+steps\s*:", raw):
            in_steps = True
            step_idx = -1
            step_indent = indent
        elif in_steps and stripped.startswith("-"):
            step_idx += 1
        if in_steps and re.search(r"\buses\s*:\s*actions/checkout@", raw):
            start_line = i
            base_indent = indent
            j = i + 1
            false_set = False
            while j < len(lines):
                nextline = lines[j].rstrip("\r\n")
                nstrip = nextline.strip()
                nindent = len(nextline) - len(nextline.lstrip(" "))
                if nstrip and nindent <= base_indent:
                    break
                if re.match(r"^\s+persist-credentials\s*:\s*false\s*(?:#.*)?$", nextline, re.I):
                    false_set = True
                j += 1
            if not false_set:
                # The analyzer highlights the `uses:` mapping, omitting the
                # list marker and preserving the line ending in the feature.
                body = lines[start_line].rstrip("\r\n")
                key_col = body.find("uses:")
                start = starts[start_line] + len(body[:key_col].encode("utf-8"))
                end_line = j - 1
                end = starts[end_line] + len(lines[end_line].encode("utf-8"))
                route = ["jobs", job, "steps", step_idx]
                loc = finding_location(filename, "does not set persist-credentials: false",
                                       route, text, start, end)
                ver = re.search(r"actions/checkout@([^\s#]+)", raw)
                severity = "Low" if ver and re.match(r"v?6(?:\.|$)", ver.group(1), re.I) else "Medium"
                out.append(finding("artipacked", "credential persistence through GitHub Actions artifacts",
                                   severity, "Low", persona, [loc]))
            i = j
        else:
            i += 1
    return out
"}

*** Update File: /workspace/output_format.py
@@
 def format_sarif(findings: list[dict], version: str = "1.25.2") -> dict:
@@

@@
                           "rules": list(rules.values())}}}]}
+
